title: Lancashire Hotpot
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb neck under a golden potato lid
excerpt: The classic northern English stew: lamb neck chops and sliced onion slow-braised in stock with a thick lid of overlapping potato slices that crisp in the oven. Left in a low oven for hours, it looks after itself.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lancashire hotpot is one of the canonical dishes of northern English working-class cooking, associated specifically with the cotton-mill towns of Lancashire. The dish was designed for the working kitchen: the ingredients were assembled in a tall earthenware pot in the morning, and the pot was placed in a low oven where it cooked slowly through the working day. The layered potato lid sealed the stew, and the top layer of potato crisped and browned where it was exposed. Traditional recipes use neck of lamb or mutton, which is cheap, fatty, and perfect for long, slow cooking; the fat dissolves to enrich the broth, and the meat becomes tender enough to eat with a spoon. Oysters were sometimes added in the original nineteenth-century versions when they were an affordable food.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 2-litre ovenproof casserole or traditional tall earthenware hotpot dish.

content.text: Slice the potatoes very thinly and evenly: thick slices stay chewy, uneven slices cook at different rates. The top layer of potato should be laid with care so the slices overlap like tiles; brush them well with butter so they brown properly. The hotpot should cook in a low oven (160 C) for the first 2 hours covered, then uncovered for 30 minutes to crisp the lid.

items.preparation: neck chops or diced neck on the bone
peeled and sliced about 3 mm thick

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C (140 C fan). Season the lamb with salt and pepper. Layer the lamb, onion, and carrot in a deep ovenproof casserole, tucking in the thyme and bay leaves. Add the Worcestershire sauce and pour the stock over. The liquid should come about halfway up the lamb; add more stock or water if needed.

Arrange the potato slices in overlapping layers over the top, seasoning each layer with salt and pepper. The final layer should be neatly tiled. Brush generously with the melted butter. Cover tightly with a lid or foil.

Bake for 2 hours covered. Remove the lid or foil, raise the temperature to 200 C (180 C fan), and bake for a further 30 minutes until the potato top is deeply golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before serving. Serve from the dish at the table.
